title: Event envelope: the outer structure shared by every event
description: The language-neutral canon of the envelope, v1. The payload (the letter) is defined per event type and validated separately (schemas/payloads/); the kernel never interprets it. Wire transport v1 is one envelope JSON per line. Optional fields are absent when unused — writers never emit null. Readers ignore unknown fields, migrate older versions on load, and refuse newer ones.

id.description: Unique id, assigned by the kernel at append time

seq.description: Stream-local sequence number, assigned at append time, starting at 1

stream.description: The stream this event belongs to, stamped by the log. The stream is the top-level container — a causally self-contained sequence with its own numbering; "conversation" and "task" are labels other layers put on streams, the kernel knows neither word.

source.description: The component instance that produced this event; "core" is reserved for kernel-recorded events

causes.description: Ids of the events that jointly triggered this one, within the same stream. Empty for root events (e.g. user input). Usually one; several when results converge into one consequence (a join). A cause may only point at an event its emitter has witnessed — enforcement layer three.

origin.description: Weak cross-stream reference, meaningful on root events: which event in which other stream provoked this stream's work. Unverified by construction — the kernel does not check it against the other stream.

reason.description: Required for decision-class events (enforced by the log per the type's registration): one sentence explaining why

payload.description: The letter — any JSON value; its schema belongs to the event type (enforcement layer four), not the envelope
